questions.question: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in direct speech. The guide said that we would be arriving in Manchester shortly.

Select the option that expresses the given sentence in direct speech.

options.html: The guide said, "We are arriving in Manchester shortly."

options.html: The guide said, "We will be arriving in Manchester shortly."

questions.solution:
The sentence in the Indirect Speech is in Conditional Continuous Tense. Therefore, the sentence in the Direct Speech will be in Future Continuous Tense.

Conditional Continuous (Subject + would/should + be + V1 +ing + Object) will be converted into Future Continuous (Subject + will/shall + be + V1 + ing + Object).

For example:

He said that he would be using the book next Friday. (Indirect Speech)

He said, "I will be using the book next Friday" (Direct Speech)

The following things in the sentence will change when changed from Indirect Speech to Direct Speech:

 'That' is removed and inverted commas ("..") are added.

 'Would' is changed into 'will'.

Therefore, the correct answer is: The guide said, "We will be arriving in Manchester shortly."

Hence, option (d) is the correct answer.

Key points:

• In the case of sentences like this where the sentence takes an Interrogative form in Direct Speech, "enquired (of)", "wanted to know", "asked", etc. in Indirect Speech is changed into "said" in Direct Speech.

• In Direct speech, the verb is always placed before the subject, unlike Indirect Speech. (That is why option (b) is incorrect)

• When changing these types of sentences from Indirect Speech to Direct Speech, "Whom" becomes "Who". (That is why option (d) is incorrect)

• For example:

o Ravi asked me whom I had visited this afternoon. (Indirect Speech)

o Ravi said to me, "Who have you visited in the afternoon?" (Direct Speech)

• The following things in the sentence will change when changed from Indirect Speech to Direct Speech:

• Therefore, the correct answer is: My mother said to me, "Who have you called last night?"

questions.question: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. When you finally let to go of the past, something better comes along.
questions.questionHtml:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

When you finally let to go of the past, something better comes along.

options.text: let to go of the past
options.html: let to go of the past

questions.solution:
The verb 'let' is used with a bare infinitive (infinitive without 'to') in active voice. Therefore, the infinitive 'to go' should be replaced with 'go' to rectify the given sentence. Hence, option (b) is the correct answer.

The correct sentence is: When you finally let go of the past, something better comes along.

Note:

Active and Passive Voice: When the person doing the action is the subject, the sentence is said to be in active form/voice. When the subject is what the action is directed at, then the sentence is said to be in passive form/voice. For example: Active Voice: Rita and her friends performed a skit. Here 'Rita and her friends' (subject) perform the action. Passive Voice: A skit was performed by Rita and her friends. Here 'skit' is the subject (at which the action is directed).

Infinitive marker: A word or affix attached to the stem of a verb in order to form the full infinitive. In English, to is the infinitive marker.

Infinitive: The infinitive is the base form of a verb, often preceded by to.

Consider the sentences given below:

· To err is human. [like a noun, the infinitive 'to err' is the subject of the verb 'is']

· My father likes to cook. [like a noun, the infinitive 'to cook' is the object of the verb 'likes']

· To vote in elections is our right. [the infinitive 'to vote', like a noun, is the subject of the verb 'is', but, like a verb, it also takes an object (elections)]

· Radha went to the lake to fetch water. [the infinitive 'to fetch', like a noun, is the object of the verb 'went', but, like a verb, it also takes an object (water)]

· The above sentences illustrate various ways in which infinitives are used. It can both act as a noun and a verb.

For example:

questions.question: Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph. A. This expansion was facilitated by their advanced chariot technology and superior weaponry. B. As they settled, the Aryans brought significant cultural and social changes. C. The Aryans settled initially in the Punjab region, utilizing its fertile land for agriculture and establishing early settlements. D. Gradually, they expanded eastward into the Gangetic plain, forming small, semi-nomadic tribal communities.
questions.questionHtml:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

A. This expansion was facilitated by their advanced chariot technology and superior weaponry.

B. As they settled, the Aryans brought significant cultural and social changes.

C. The Aryans settled initially in the Punjab region, utilizing its fertile land for agriculture and establishing early settlements.

D. Gradually, they expanded eastward into the Gangetic plain, forming small, semi-nomadic tribal communities.
questions.solution:
After reading all the sentences thoroughly, we can determine the logical order. Sentence C should hold the first position, as it introduces where the Aryans initially settled and describes their early activities in the Punjab region. Sentence D should follow sentence C because it gives the details of their gradual eastward expansion into the Gangetic plain, showing the progression of their settlements. Sentence A comes next, explaining how the Aryans' advanced chariot technology and superior weaponry facilitated their expansion, building upon the context provided in sentences 'C' and 'D'. Finally, sentence B concludes the paragraph by discussing the significant cultural and social changes brought by the Aryans as they settled in various regions.

Therefore, the right order is CDAB. This sequence provides a coherent flow from initial settlement and expansion, utilization of resources to technological advancements and finally, the cultural impact of the Aryans. Hence, (b) is the correct answer.

The Champions League was won by Real Madrid. (Passive Voice)

The subject of the Active Voice is changed into the object of the Passive voice. Also, the object of the Active Voice is changed into the subject of the Passive Voice.

The usage of a 'to be' form of verb is necessary while changing the voice of the sentence from Active to Passive.

The preposition "by" is used before the object made in Passive Voice. However, it is optional in some cases.

The question in Active voice is in interrogative form. These are "wh" questions that don't take "yes" or "no" as an answer.

"Which/ What" etc are placed as they are.

For example:

What are you doing? (Active)

What is being done by you? (Passive)

But, when "Which/What" is used as a subject in Active voice, it is changed into "By what" in Passive voice.

For example:

What makes you happy? (Active)

By what are you made happy? (Passive)

Also, the sentence is in the Past Indefinite in the Active voice. So, in the Passive voice, Past Indefinite tense should be used.

In the given sentence, two plural subjects are joined by 'and'. So, we have to use a plural verb.

The options except (b) don't follow the correct grammatical format of the Passive Voice.

Thus, the correct answer is: Why were my terms and conditions not agreed to by you?

questions.question: How many squares are in kho-kho court? खो-खो कोर्ट में कितने वर्ग होते हैं?
questions.solution:
In a kho-kho court, there are 8 squares marked on the central lane.

A kho-kho court consists of a rectangular field measuring 29 meters in length and 16 meters in width.

There is a central lane (lengthwise) that divides the court into two halves.

On the central lane, 8 small squares are marked. Each square is used for the positioning of chasers during the game.

These squares are essential to the gameplay, as they serve as designated areas for players to squat and participate in the game strategically.

Terminologies used in Kho-kho:

Kho, cross lane, Free zone, pole dive, court, square, tapping, extra period, active Chaser, inning, fake kho, central lane, poles, minus kho, late kho.

The President of India may enact ordinances under Article 123 of the Indian Constitution.

This article states that the President may promulgate an ordinance even while the Parliament is not in session if he is certain that circumstances exist that need him to act immediately.

Although the ordinance must be presented to both Houses of Parliament and expires six weeks after the reassembly of Parliament or sooner if the Parliament does not accept it, it has the same power and effect as an act of Parliament.

Further insights:

Article 77: This article deals with the conduct of business of the Government of India. It states that all executive actions of the Government of India shall be expressed to be taken in the name of the President.

Article 111: This article deals with the presentation of Bills in Parliament. It states that a Bill shall not be deemed to have been passed by the Houses of Parliament unless it has been presented to the President and has received his assent. The President may give his assent to the Bill, withhold his assent, or return the Bill for reconsideration.

Article 143: This article deals with the powers of the Supreme Court to advise the President on any matter of public importance. The President may consult the Supreme Court on any question of law or fact which he may refer to it. The Supreme Court shall give its opinion on the matter referred to it.

The major highlights of the Census 2011 (Provisional figures) are as under ;-

· The population of India has increased by more than 181 million(18.1 crore) during the decade 2001-2011.

· Uttar Pradesh (199.5 million) is the most populous State in the country followed by Maharashtra with 112 million.

· The percentage decadal growth rates of the six most populous States have declined during 2001-2011 compared to 1991-2001:

- Uttar Pradesh (25.85% to 20.09%)

- Maharashtra (22.73% to 15.99%)

- Bihar (28.62% to 25.07%)

- West Bengal (17.77 % to 13.93%)

- Andhra Pradesh (14.59% to 11.10%)

- Madhya Pradesh (24.26% to 20.30%)

· 15 States/UTs have grown by less than 1.5 per cent per annum during 2001-2011, while the number of such States/UTs was only 4 during the previous decade.

· During 2001-2011, as many as 25 States/UTs with a share of about 85% of the country's population registered an annual growth rate of less than 2% as compared to, 15 States/UTs with a share of about 42% during the period 1991-2001.

· The total number of children in the age-group 0-6 is 158.8 million (-5 million since 2001)

· Twenty States and Union Territories now have over one million children in the age group 0-6 years. On the other extreme, there are five States and Union Territories in the country that are yet to reach the one hundred thousand mark.

· Three major States (J&K, Bihar & Gujarat) have shown decline in sex ratio as compared to Census 2001.

· Kerala with 1084 has the highest sex ratio followed by Puducherry with 1038, Daman & Diu has the lowest sex ratio of 618.

· Child sex ratio (0-6 years) is 914. Increasing trend in the child sex ratio (0-6) seen in Punjab, Haryana, Himachal Pradesh, Gujarat, Tamil Nadu, Mizoram and A&N Islands. In all remaining 27 States/UTs, the child sex ratio show decline over Census 2001.

• Revenue Deficit arises when the government's revenue expenditure exceeds its revenue receipts.
